title: git: Factor out dissect_pkt_line helper
description:
Add dissect_pkt_line helper that dissects a single pkt-line and
simplifies the pre-existing dissect_git_pdu().

A later patch will make use of this same helper for HTTP support.

Part of #17093

notes.body: changed the description
mentioned in merge request !1946
This change seems to conflict with !1922. Please rebase it so we can start review.

If the purpose is to read the packet line by line (as used in !1946) then you should not have the calls to col_set_str(), this proto_tree_add_item() and the proto_item_add_subtree() in this function but in the parent one (and actually the col_set_str calls are already done in dissect_git_pdu().

changed this line in [version 5 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1942/diffs?diff_id=141271511&start_sha=04e00838080b220a7f71502599e9df77fcbd25d1#af0057bee6b1c65490fa9248f7a79e62a59dd7a2_102_102)

Removed the `col_set_str()` calls from `dissect_pkt_line()` but kept `proto_tree_add_item()` and the `proto_item_add_subtree()` in ln 103-104 for their use in the `proto_tree_add_uint()`s, is this right?

No, for several reasons:
* proto_git is supposed to indicate the presence of a Git PDU not a part of a Git PDU
* You are using the length till the end of the PDU (the -1 parameter) instead of the pkt-line length

If you want an item representing the pkt-line, introduce a new hf_git_pkt_line or similar variable.

Can this comment give a description of this new helper: what arguments it takes, what the return value is, and what it does? Such a comment can make it easier to read and understand calling code because then you get a sense of what the function call is supposed to accomplish without having to read the function body.

changed this line in [version 13 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1942/diffs?diff_id=143180994&start_sha=68dc2268d61166a2be9803020b23594315cb2a46#af0057bee6b1c65490fa9248f7a79e62a59dd7a2_95_95)

From the commit message:

> Depends on MR !1922

Please remove this line: this kind of dependency information is conveyed by what commits it depends on instead.
Either you return the number of consumed bytes so as to do offset += dissect_pkt_line(), or you increment the offset variable in the dissect_pkt_line() function, but you should not do both.

This looks ready to mark as not a WIP any more.

Also, it's probably a good time to revisit the commit message: e.g., something like `git: factor out dissect_pkt_line helper that dissects a single pkt-line` might be easier to understand. In the commit message body it can mention that a later patch will make use of this same helper for HTTP support (since that helps the reader understand the motivation behind the change).
